english: Let $N=\displaystyle\prod_{k=1}^{10}\dfrac{(2k)!}{k!}$. Then the greatest non-negative integer $m$ such that $2^{m}$ divides $N$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $N=\displaystyle\prod_{k=1}^{10}\dfrac{(2k)!}{k!}$ है। तब वह महत्तम अऋणात्मक पूर्णांक $m$, जिसके लिए $2^{m}$, $N$ को विभाजित करता है, ______ है।
solution: $\Rightarrow\dfrac{(2k)!}{k!}=2^{k}\cdot(\text{odd number})$, so its exponent of 2 is exactly $k$
solution_full: Split $(2k)!$ into its even and odd factors: $(2k)!=\left[2\cdot4\cdot6\cdots(2k)\right]\cdot\left[1\cdot3\cdot5\cdots(2k-1)\right]$.
The even part is $2^{k}(1\cdot2\cdots k)=2^{k}\,k!$. Hence $\dfrac{(2k)!}{k!}=2^{k}\cdot\left[1\cdot3\cdots(2k-1)\right]$, and the bracket is a product of odd numbers, so it is odd.
Therefore the exponent of 2 in $\dfrac{(2k)!}{k!}$ is exactly $k$.

The same follows from Legendre's formula: $e_{2}((2k)!)=\sum_{j\geq1}\left[\dfrac{2k}{2^{j}}\right]=k+\sum_{j\geq1}\left[\dfrac{k}{2^{j}}\right]=k+e_{2}(k!)$. For example, $k=10$: $e_{2}(20!)=10+5+2+1=18$, $e_{2}(10!)=5+2+1=8$, difference $10$.
Exponents add over a product, so the exponent of 2 in $N$ is $\sum_{k=1}^{10}k=55$. Hence $m=55$.
originality_note: New: the exponent of 2 in a product of central ratios (2k)!/k!, where splitting (2k)! into even and odd parts (or Legendre's formula) shows each factor contributes exactly k, turning the problem into an arithmetic series (way 4: an invariant that makes a messy product clean). Closest known: exponent of 2 in 50! or in C(2n,n). Different because: the product of ten factorial ratios collapses by a per-factor invariant.
